summary: CLI key-broker login hangs after Okta auth cookie truncation by edge proxy
description: Multiple engineers reported that the internal CLI key-broker process hangs during SSO login. The broker initiates Okta OIDC flow, receives redirect with session cookie, then stalls waiting for token exchange. Issue started after edge-proxy upgrade (cookie header trimming) and affects teams using the CLI for runbook and deployment actions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use latest internal CLI (v2.14.0) on macOS or Linux
3) CLI opens browser for Okta SSO, authenticate with corporate SSO
4) Okta redirects back to localhost callback; edge-proxy forwards request to key-broker service
5) Key-broker stalls at "`/auth/callback`" waiting for cookie/token exchange; no tokens returned
observed_behavior: Login window opens but CLI spinner continues indefinitely
No service account token is returned to CLI
Browser shows successful redirect to localhost callback with 200 from key-broker
Key-broker logs show cookie header length mismatch and then no token exchange attempt
expected_behavior: Key-broker completes OIDC code exchange and returns short-lived service token to CLI
CLI prints 'Login successful' and persists local credential
logs: 2026-03-10T15:04:12Z key-broker auth:recv callback request id=3f2a7 - Cookie header length=8192
2026-03-10T15:04:12Z edge-proxy http:trim_cookie - original Cookie header truncated to 4096 bytes by set-cookie-sanitizer
2026-03-10T15:04:12Z key-broker auth:error - missing 'session' claim in cookie, aborting exchange id=3f2a7
investigation_notes: Initial report from infra team coincided with edge-proxy 2.8.1 rollout that enabled a cookie trimming filter

Hypothesis: proxy truncation removed Okta session cookie (cookie size exceeded 4k) which prevented key-broker from validating session claim; broker code treats missing claim as unrecoverable and stalls waiting for callback
Reproduced in staging by enabling CookieTrim filter on edge-proxy and running CLI login; observed identical log pattern
Confirmed browser receives full redirect URL including code, but key-broker fails before initiating token exchange due to malformed cookie parse path

Temporary change: key-broker retry path added to treat missing cookie as 'continue-with-code' allowing token exchange; workaround requires broker change and additional validation against Okta introspect endpoint
Security review: bypassing cookie validation has risk; must ensure code verifier is validated to avoid CSRF. Will pair SRE + security on mitigation design.
impact_summary: ~25 engineers across infra, security, and SRE affected (unable to obtain CLI tokens)
Blocking runbook access and short-term operational tasks relying on key-broker tokens
Ticket flagged for on-call escalation due to P1 business impact
comments: 2026-03-10 15:25 - Aisha Patel (Support): We've scoped this as P1. Captured logs from affected hosts and escalated to proxy on-call.
2026-03-10 16:10 - SRE-OnCall: Verified edge-proxy 2.8.1 introduced CookieTrim filter. Rolled back filter on us-west canary; observed successful logins from 3 test users.

2026-03-11 09:02 - Samira Khan (Assignee): Implemented a safe retry in key-broker to attempt OIDC code exchange when cookie parse fails. Deployed in staging behind feature flag. Awaiting security sign-off.

2026-03-12 11:44 - Diego Martinez (Security): Reviewed retry path; requires additional PKCE verification. Security OK with PKCE verification and token introspection added. Planning prod rollout after canary.
2026-03-12 14:20 - Liam Nguyen (Reporter): Confirmed workaround allows CLI login in staging; will validate with broader team tomorrow.
next_steps: 1) SRE to perform controlled canary rollout of key-broker fix (with PKCE verification) in us-west
2) Edge-proxy team to patch CookieTrim filter to preserve Okta session cookies or increase header size threshold
3) Security to complete sign-off and update runbook for cookie-truncation scenarios
4) Postmortem scheduled after mitigation: capture scope, timeline, and permanent fix plan
workarounds: Users can: 1) use browser-based personal access token (PAT) for short-term operations, or 2) re-run login from a host behind an unaffected ingress that doesn't trim cookies
Edge-proxy rollback to previous config restores full functionality for affected hosts
resolution: Mitigation in staging validated. Awaiting controlled canary rollout to prod and edge-proxy config patch. Temporary workarounds available. Postmortem to follow after prod rollout.
resolution_notes: Key-broker updated to not fail on missing cookie if valid OIDC code and PKCE verifier are present; edge-proxy team will release patch to CookieTrim filter. Follow-up: add telemetry to detect cookie truncation events and alert earlier.
